claims.text: Dynamically reversible surface hydroxide/oxide formation governs the high activity of nanoscale PGM catalysts during ethanol oxidation.
Dynamically reversible surface hydroxide/oxide formation governs product selectivity during ethanol oxidation.
Dynamically reversible surface hydroxide/oxide formation governs catalyst durability during ethanol oxidation.
Surface hydroxide/oxide species facilitate the multi-electron and proton-transfer steps of ethanol oxidation.
The baseline catalyst surface is moderately oxidized, with a balanced mixture of metallic and oxide/hydroxide sites in neutral or weakly alkaline electrolyte.
Changing electrolyte pH or potential-hold conditions changes the in situ surface oxidation state and the abundance of surface hydroxide species.
Local pH and potential changes dynamically alter the PGM surface oxidation state under ethanol-oxidation conditions.
Active surface hydroxide species assist C–C bond breaking in ethanol.
Active surface hydroxide species assist C–H bond breaking in ethanol.
Metallic surface sites provide electron conduction needed for high catalytic performance.
Oxide/hydroxide sites facilitate proton transfer and stabilize reaction intermediates.
An optimal balance of metallic and oxide/hydroxide sites is necessary for high catalytic performance and durability.
Slightly increasing pH or applying a more oxidizing potential will enhance surface hydroxide formation.
Enhanced surface hydroxide formation will increase ethanol-oxidation current density.
Enhanced surface hydroxide formation will improve selectivity toward complete ethanol-oxidation products.
Suppressing surface hydroxide formation will reduce catalytic activity and selectivity.
Very high pH or overly oxidizing potentials can produce excessive oxide and deactivate the catalyst.
Excessive oxide formation can reduce metallic conductivity or cause irreversible surface changes.
